title: ✨ What if I told you that preparing for pregnancy isn’t just a woman’s responsibility?
instagramCaption:
✨ What if I told you that preparing for pregnancy isn’t just a woman’s responsibility?

We’ve normalized telling women to start folic acid, eat healthier, exercise, and avoid harmful habits before trying to conceive.

But how often do we tell future dads to prepare too?

The truth is, conception is a team effort.

Emerging research shows that a father’s health before conception may influence sperm quality, early embryo development, placental function, and even aspects of a child’s long-term health through epigenetic changes. This doesn’t change the baby’s DNA, but it may influence how certain genes are expressed.

The encouraging part? Sperm is constantly being produced and takes around 70–90 days to mature. That means the habits a man builds in the 3 months before conception can influence the quality of the sperm involved in conception.

This isn’t about placing pressure or blame on fathers.

It’s about recognizing that both parents have an opportunity to support a healthier pregnancy before it even begins. Preconception care should be a conversation for couples.. not just women.

title: You’re taking your prenatal supplements… but are they actually getting absorbed? 🤰🏻💊👀
instagramCaption:
You’re taking your prenatal supplements… but are they actually getting absorbed? 🤰🏻💊👀

Pregnancy nutrition isn’t just about what goes in.. 
it’s about what actually gets absorbed, utilised, and reaches your baby.

And physiologically, a lot is happening behind the scenes ⬇️

→ Your gut absorption isn’t constant during pregnancy
Hormonal shifts (hello progesterone) slow gastric motility →
nutrients sit longer, absorption becomes inconsistent, bloating increases
So some days you feel great… some days, not so much

→ Minerals share the same transport pathways
Inside your intestine, nutrients like iron, calcium, zinc use overlapping carriers
→ If they arrive together, they literally compete at a cellular level
Result? Lower net absorption despite “taking everything”

→ Your body prioritises the baby first
Even with borderline intake, fetal requirements are maintained
→ Which means you may feel the fatigue, weakness, cramps first

→ Muscle + tissue demand increases silently
As your body adapts (posture changes, weight shifts),
your nutritional needs aren’t just for baby but also for your musculoskeletal system
→ This is why some women feel unexpected aches, low strength, slower recovery

So if you’ve been thinking,
“I’m eating well, taking supplements… why do I still feel this way?”
there’s a real physiological reason behind it.

Let’s make pregnancy feel better, not just look “normal” on reports.

title: Most couples start preparing for pregnancy by focusing on the woman’s body.
instagramCaption:
Most couples start preparing for pregnancy by focusing on the woman’s body.
And while that’s important… it’s only half the picture.

Male fertility isn’t just about sperm count.
It’s also about sperm DNA quality, which plays a role in fertilisation, embryo development, and even early pregnancy stability.

What many people don’t realise ⤵️
• Sperm DNA damage has been linked with lower implantation rates
• Heat exposure (laptops on lap, tight underwear, long sitting hours) can affect sperm production
• Being overweight can alter hormone balance → impacting sperm quality
• Even moderate alcohol + chronic stress can reduce motility and morphology over time

And here’s something important:
Male fertility is modifiable.
Unlike many female factors, small lifestyle changes over a few months can actually improve sperm health.

Which means..
Preconception care is not about doing more…
It’s about doing it together.

If you’re trying to conceive (or planning to), this is your reminder to approach it as a team, physically, mentally, and medically.

title: Most women focus on when to get pregnant… but very few focus on whether their body is actually ready.
instagramCaption:
Most women focus on when to get pregnant… but very few focus on whether their body is actually ready. 

➡️ Fertility isn’t a switch that turns on when you decide.
It’s a function your body allows when it feels safe, nourished, and regulated.

And your brain is constantly assessing that.

🔅For example —

If you’re constantly tired, under-eating, over-exercising, or stressed…
your body doesn’t see that as “normal life”

It sees it as stress or survival mode‼️

And in that state, reproduction is not a priority.

This is controlled by a hormonal system called the HPO axis (brain ↔ ovaries communication).

🔸When this communication is smooth → ovulation happens regularly
When it’s disrupted → ovulation can get delayed, irregular, or even stop temporarily

❓What’s important to understand is:

This doesn’t always show up dramatically.
Sometimes it’s subtle like:
• Slightly longer cycles
• Delayed ovulation
• Low energy
• Feeling “off” but ignoring it

Your body is not working against you
It’s responding to what you’re consistently doing

So instead of asking:
“Why is this not happening?”

Shift to:
“Is my body getting what it needs to support this?”

Small changes in your daily routine can bring your system back into balance..
and that’s where real fertility support begins ✨

• Allows the pelvis to adapt to different labor positions
• Supports optimal fetal positioning and descent
• Reduces unnecessary muscle guarding and tension
• Improves coordination between the hips, spine, and pelvic floor
• Helps the pelvic floor lengthen and respond appropriately during birth

These movements are commonly used in evidence-based prenatal physiotherapy because they encourage mobility over rigidity which is a key requirement for physiological labor.

Did you know that strength training during pregnancy can lead to smoother, shorter, and less complicated labor? Here’s how:

✅ Shorter Labor: Stronger muscles improve endurance, helping with efficient contractions and pushing. Women who strength train often have shorter first and second stages of labor.

✅ Lower C-Section Risk: Strengthening the core and pelvic muscles promotes better fetal positioning, reducing complications that lead to C-sections.

✅ Less Pain & Epidural Use: Strength training enhances endurance and pain tolerance, making labor more manageable with less need for pain relief.

✅ Fewer Forceps/Vacuum Deliveries: A strong pelvic floor improves pushing effectiveness, lowering the need for assisted deliveries.

✅ Reduced Tearing & Faster Recovery: Strength training improves muscle control and flexibility, decreasing perineal tears and supporting faster postpartum healing.

Strong moms, strong births! Stay active, move smart, and prepare your body for labor.

Baby is lying sideways in the womb. This position often requires assistance closer to delivery.

The hormone relaxin prepares your body for childbirth but can overstretch and destabilize the pelvic joint, causing discomfort.

Many women think it’s just “normal pregnancy pain” 🛑 - but it’s NOT! 
With the right care, PSD can be managed effectively.

🔍Essential Blood Tests for PCOS – Tailoring Your Health Journey!🔍

Managing PCOS isn’t a one-size-fits-all approach. Different blood tests may be recommended based on your unique symptoms, health history, and goals. 
Here’s why they matter:

1️⃣ Hormone Profile: Helps uncover hormonal imbalances affecting your cycle, ovulation, and androgen levels - key for diagnosing and managing PCOS.

2️⃣ Blood Sugar & Insulin: PCOS often impacts insulin sensitivity, so these tests check for insulin resistance and diabetes risk.

3️⃣ Thyroid Function: Thyroid disorders can mimic PCOS symptoms, so testing ensures symptoms aren’t thyroid-related.

4️⃣ Lipid Profile: PCOS can increase cardiovascular risks, making heart health tests essential.

5️⃣ Nutrient Levels: Vitamins D, B12, and iron are often low in PCOS, impacting energy, immunity, and mood.

6️⃣ Inflammatory Markers: CRP and ESR reveal inflammation levels, which can worsen PCOS symptoms.

7️⃣ Liver Enzymes: PCOS can affect liver health, especially with fatty liver risks, so monitoring ALT and AST is crucial.

🔅Each test supports a personalized treatment plan - because what works for one person may not work for another. 
❗️Tailoring care helps target your unique symptoms and health goals more effectively!

🔸Sleep Disturbances 
🔸Mood Swings 
🔸Decreased Bone Density 
🔸Metabolic Changes 

Why Exercise Matters:

1. Bone Density: Weight-bearing exercises help maintain bone density, which decreases as estrogen levels drop. This is essential to lower osteoporosis risk.

2. Mood Support: Exercise releases endorphins that naturally improve mood and reduce symptoms of anxiety or depression. These benefits are especially helpful in managing climacteric mood swings.

3. Sleep Quality: Regular aerobic activity has been shown to enhance sleep quality, a major relief for those experiencing menopause-related sleep disturbances.

4. Metabolic Balance: Exercise supports healthy weight and regulates metabolism, reducing the risk of weight gain and insulin resistance during menopause.

5. Heart Health: Cardiovascular exercise strengthens heart function, essential as cardiovascular risks can increase after menopause.

title: 🔆Managing labor pain effectively is crucial for a smoother birthing experience🤰🏻
instagramCaption:
🔆Managing labor pain effectively is crucial for a smoother birthing experience🤰🏻

🖋️Here are 5 evidence-based techniques that can make a significant difference:

🔸 Upright Position and Movement: Staying upright and mobile during labor allows gravity to assist in fetal descent, enhancing uterine contractions and reducing pressure on the lower back. Positions like squatting or leaning forward can help optimize the baby’s position and alleviate pain.
🔸 Breathing Techniques: Controlled breathing, such as diaphragmatic breathing or patterned techniques, plays a pivotal role in pain management. These techniques promote relaxation, reduce anxiety, and ensure efficient oxygenation for both mother and baby.
🔸 Perineal Massage: Regular perineal massage in the weeks leading up to labor can increase the elasticity of the perineal tissues, potentially reducing the risk of tears and the need for episiotomy.
🔸 Hydrotherapy: Immersing yourself in warm water during labor, such as in a birthing pool, can significantly reduce pain perception. The buoyancy and warmth relax the muscles, ease contractions, and provide a soothing environment for labor.
🔸 TENS (Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation): TENS is a non-invasive method that uses low-voltage electrical currents to block pain signals and stimulate the release of endorphins. Applying a TENS unit to the lower back during labor can provide effective pain relief, especially in the early stages.

‼️For more details on these techniques, reach out to a women’s health physiotherapist to help you prepare for a more comfortable labor.😇

title: Women who have recently given birth are frequently advised to wear abdominal binders or post-partum belts.

Women who have recently given birth are frequently advised to wear abdominal binders or post-partum belts.

➡️In India, it was and still is common practice to wrap a long piece of cloth (cotton saree) tightly around the lower abdomen. Many claim that doing so reduces the bulging belly and flattens the stomach in a matter of months, but is this true?

✨According to studies, these belts can be beneficial for providing some support to the back and abdominal muscles, which can eventually improve posture which is TRUE, but the rest of the claims are false.

Let us clear up some misconceptions -

1) Binding helps the abdominal organs and uterus return to their original positions faster - NO, because the uterus is a muscular organ that returns to its original position on its own in 6 weeks. Its recovery is aided by a healthy diet and regular exercise.

2) Improves abdominal muscle tone and gives a flat stomach - A binder will not strengthen or tone the muscles rather it just provides support.

3) Aids in pelvic floor recovery - False, because if the organs are compressed by the belt, it adds pressure to their already weak pelvic floor.

Wearing it too tightly can cause hernias or prolapse, as well as restrict breathing.

📌Post-partum binders are not the answer to a flat or toned stomach. What really helps for optimum healing and building a good post-partum body is proper diet and exercise, as well as an appointment with a Women's Health Physiotherapist.

🧐How do you know that you have a Hypertonic or Hypotonic Pelvic floor?? 

The terms HYPERTONIC and HYPOTONIC are used to describe the state of the pelvic floor muscles.

➡️A Hypertonic pelvic floor is a condition in which the muscles of the pelvic floor are overly tight and lack flexibility. Chronic pelvic pain, pain during intercourse, difficulty urinating or having bowel movements, can all result from this.
Also, remember just because a muscle is TIGHT does not make it STRONG!!

➡️Hypotonic pelvic floor, on the other hand, is a condition in which the muscles of the pelvic floor are weak and lack tone or contraction. This can result in symptoms such as urinary or faecal incontinence, pelvic organ prolapse, and decreased sexual sensation.

➡️It's important to note that these conditions can also coexist in some individuals, where certain areas of the pelvic floor may be hypertonic while others may be hypotonic.

📌Treatment for either condition may involve pelvic floor physical therapy, which can help improve muscle tone, relax the overactive muscles, improve flexibility, and strength depending on the cause and symptoms!

📌Wash your hands - 
Dirty hands can spread harmful bacteria to your genital area, causing infection.

📌Sterilize the cup - 
To avoid bacterial growth and infection, menstrual cups should be thoroughly cleaned with a steriliser after each use.

➡️Advantages of using a Menstrual cup:

📝It is important to note that folic acid supplementation does not say with absolute certainty the prevention of NTDs, but it can minimize the likelihood significantly.

title: The PELVIC FLOOR is a group of muscles, ligaments, and connective tissues in the pelvis that form a hammock-like stru…
instagramCaption:
The PELVIC FLOOR is a group of muscles, ligaments, and connective tissues in the pelvis that form a hammock-like structure. It runs from the pubic bone in the front of the pelvis to the tailbone in the back and the sit bones on either side.

It serves several functions, including:

📌STABILIZATION: The pelvic floor muscles works with the abdominal and back muscles to keep the pelvis and spine stable.

📌CONTINENCE: The pelvic floor muscles team up with the sphincter muscles to control the urethra, anus, and vaginal opening and closing. A strong and coordinated pelvic floor helps to prevent urine, gas, and faeces leakage.

📌PREGNANCY AND CHILDBIRTH: Pelvic floor supports the growing foetus and uterus during pregnancy. It stretches during childbirth to allow the baby to pass through the birth canal. Pelvic floor strengthening before and after childbirth can help prevent pelvic floor disorders.

📌PROLAPSE: The pelvic floor supports the pelvic organs, including the bladder, uterus, and rectum. These organs can prolapse or descend into the vaginal or rectal area if they are not supported. 

📌SEXUAL FUNCTION: Pelvic floor disorders occur as a result of either overactive or underactive pelvic floor muscles. Both situations can lead to sexual dysfunction in both men and women.

➡️In conclusion, maintaining and strengthening/relaxing the pelvic floor properly can aid in the prevention or treatment of Pelvic Floor Dysfunctions.

title: Missing your period is one of the most obvious signs of pregnancy, but getting a positive pregnancy test is the only …
instagramCaption:
Missing your period is one of the most obvious signs of pregnancy, but getting a positive pregnancy test is the only way to be certain.

Pregnancy tests come in a variety of forms, including simple strips, sticks, and digital tests.

Digital tests are fairly self-explanatory and leave little room for interpretation with a yes or no response.
However, the strip and sticks can frequently leave you wondering what a faint line means!
Because there is detectable hCG hormone present, the line can be faint and you are pregnant.

If the line is very faint it can mean that you are very early in your pregnancy because there is a low concentration of hCG.

You are still pregnant if you know you missed your period several days or weeks ago and notice a faint line.
However, this could be a sign that you are miscarrying because the hCG in your urine should have increased exponentially by now and produced a dark line.

The interaction of oxygen on the test may cause an EVAPORATION LINE to appear after the urine has evaporated from the stick, resulting in a FALSE POSITIVE result.
The good news is that the evaporation line appears only if you have exceeded the time limit for reading the test (usually 3-5 minutes).

Always visit your Gynecologist without hesitation if you are in doubt.
The sooner your Gynecologist diagnoses you, the better you will understand your situation and the reason for it.

Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a hormonal disorder that affects millions of women around the world. PCOS can cause symptoms such as irregular menstrual cycles, weight gain, acne, and infertility. Exercise can help to regulate hormonal imbalances, reduce insulin resistance, and improve overall health, making it an important part of PCOS management. As a physiotherapist, I recommend the following PCOS exercises:

📌CARDIOVASCULAR EXERCISE, such as brisk walking, cycling, or swimming, is important for lowering the risk of heart disease and improving insulin resistance. On most days of the week, aim for at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity cardiovascular exercise.

📌STRENGTH TRAINING, such as weightlifting or resistance band workouts, can help to increase muscle mass and improve insulin sensitivity. Aim for at least two to three days of strength training per week.

📌HIGH-INTENSITY INTERVAL TRAINING (HIIT) is a type of exercise that consists of short bursts of intense exercise followed by rest periods. HIIT can be especially effective at lowering insulin resistance and increasing overall fitness levels. It is important, however, to begin slowly and gradually increase the intensity and duration of the workouts.

📌PILATES is a low-impact exercise that can help to strengthen core muscles, improve posture, and reduce stress levels.

📌YOGA can be especially beneficial for women with PCOS because it can help to reduce stress, improve insulin sensitivity, and regulate menstrual cycles.

Individualized approach: It is critical to tailor the exercise prescription to the needs and preferences of the individual. A Women's Health Physiotherapist can work with the individual to develop a personalised exercise plan that takes their fitness level, medical history, and lifestyle factors into account.

NOTE - Exercise should be part of a comprehensive PCOS treatment plan that includes dietary changes, medication, and other lifestyle changes.
Before beginning any new exercise programme, consult with your Gynecologist or a Women's Health Physiotherapist.

The following are some of the conditions for which you should see a women's health physiotherapist.

It also helps you prepare for childbirth.

4) PELVIC FLOOR DYSFUNCTION - A hypotone or hypertone pelvic floor can cause urinary/fecal incontinence, uterine prolapse, or sexual problems. Depending on the cause and symptoms, a WHP can prescribe exercises to treat the patient.

5) POST ABDOMINAL/GYNAE SURGERY - Exercises can help you regain your functional self after a surgery such as a C-section or a Hysterectomy (removal of uterus).

6) MENOPAUSAL SYMPTOMS - Exercise has been shown to be effective in treating menopausal symptoms such as stress, weight gain, and decreased bone mass density.

title: Ideally, you should begin seeing your gynaecologist in your early adolescence so that you can develop a trusting rela…
instagramCaption:
Ideally, you should begin seeing your gynaecologist in your early adolescence so that you can develop a trusting relationship with your doctor in the long run. Certain changes in your body may become apparent as you age. Here are some warning signs to look out for:

1) DYSMENORRHEA - This is one of the most common symptoms experienced by women. It is described as severe cramping. It is usually the result of prostaglandin release. Prostaglandin causes the muscles of the uterus to contract, causing discomfort and pain. The level of intensity varies from person to person.

2) IRREGULAR MENSES - This usually occurs in adolescents who are just starting their period as their bodies adjust to hormonal changes. A normal cycle lasts 21-35 days; any cycle that lasts less than 21 days or more than 35 days is considered abnormal.

3) EXCESSIVE BLEEDING - Also known as "Menorrhagia" in the medical world. It is a condition in which period flow lasts for more than 7 days or heavy bleeding necessitates frequent pad/tampon changes throughout the day, which can be caused by uterine polyp, fibroid, adenomyosis, endometriosis, and other conditions.

4) FERTILITY CONCERNS - One in every seven couples may have difficulty conceiving. Common causes include irregular ovulation (PCOS), poor quality sperm, a blocked or damaged fallopian tube, and so on. Age, overweight/underweight, alcohol/smoking abuse, stress, and other risk factors all have an impact on fertility.

5) STDs - All sexually active women should be tested for STDs on a regular basis. This allows for the early detection and immediate prevention of a variety of health conditions.

6) MENOPAUSAL SYMPTOMS - These include mood swings, body aches, constipation, hot flushes, night sweats, and other symptoms. Although most women do not require treatment for the symptoms, they may be uncomfortable for some.

7) BREAST PROBLEMS - Breast problems such as lumps, pain or tenderness in the breast, nipple discharge or inversion, and changes in the skin of the breast are common in women of all ages. While it can be frightening, breast cancer is not the cause of the majority of problems.
